title: Trainstorm Script Primitives (Generation IR) — v2
description: The SEMANTIC generation layer: an ordered array of didactic moves emitted from source material, BEFORE presentation. Each primitive is a typed knowledge structure. Primitives are realized DOWNSTREAM into presentation elements. Governed, closed vocabulary — a new primitive type requires a version bump. V2 CHANGE (ratified 2026-07-24, unification-map §4 / CONFLICT-01): knowledge_check moves from enumerated options to RESPONSE-FEATURE form — it describes what a correct response must CONTAIN (expected_response_features) and what learners are predicted to get wrong (misconception_predictions, structured with IDs and confidence). MC/MR/TF/matching/sequence become RENDERS of it: the realizer generates options at realization time — the key from expected_response_features, distractors from misconception_predictions via a divergent pass. The 11 primitive types are unchanged from v1. ADDITIVE UPDATE (2026-07-27): every primitive type now carries an optional teaches field. Fixes a real gap: which objective a primitive serves was previously decided twice — once implicitly, when the Generator drafts toward a locked objective, and again explicitly when the realized element's intent.teaches is filled in — with nothing forcing the two to agree. The Generator now stamps teaches once, at draft time; the Realizer relays it forward rather than re-deciding. Optional, not required, because a few types (closure especially) legitimately span more than one objective rather than serving one. This is additive, not breaking — existing v2 instances that omit teaches remain valid — so it ships in place; no v3, no second file. Checking that a primitive's teaches actually matches its realized element's is a tools/lint.py rule, not yet built.

misconceptionPrediction.description: A falsifiable prior about learner error, stated before any learner is observed. IDs are stable (mc_ prefix, minted at generation, never positional) so the Responsive Engine can later place posteriors over them and the realizer can trace each rendered distractor to the misconception it operationalizes.

claim.description: What learners are predicted to wrongly believe or do, stated as a claim about cognition — not as answer-option text.

confidence.description: Prior confidence that this misconception is prevalent in the target segment. Seeds the evidence loop.

source.description: Where the prediction comes from: audience-model entry (segment × objective), SME input, or observed data.

feedback.description: Remediation shown when a learner's response evidences THIS misconception. Realizes into per-distractor feedback.

knowledge_check.description: V2 FORM — a check for understanding in RESPONSE-FEATURE form. Describes what a correct response must contain, not lettered options. Options are a RENDER: the realizer generates them at realization time (key from expected_response_features; distractors from misconception_predictions via the Generator's divergent pass, with parity constraints — vocabulary, register, length). Render targets choose form (MC/MR/TF/matching/sequence) and capacity (Storyline supports up to 10 choices) as render parameters, not schema facts. If a client or SME mandates fixed verbatim options, that is a render-time constraint recorded against the render target — the primitive stays semantic. Migration from v1: each v1 options[correct=true] label maps into expected_response_features; each incorrect label is restated as the misconception it evidences.

prompt.description: The question or task, semantically stated. Single-concept; the realizer enforces form rules per target.

expected_response_features.description: What a correct response must contain or demonstrate — competency-aligned features, not option text. The semantic key.

misconception_predictions.description: Structured priors about learner error. Distractors are generated FROM these — never invented alongside the key.

feedback_incorrect.description: Default remediation when no specific misconception is matched. Misconception-specific feedback lives on each prediction.

source_reference.description: Citation into the source store (authoritative band) grounding this check. Provenance per check — the profiles' discipline, kept.

teaches.description: objective_ids this primitive was drafted toward. For knowledge_check especially, this is the field that should have prevented drift: the check's teaches and the realized element's intent.teaches are testing whether the same objective was meant both times.

boundary_statement.description: Scope, limits, caveats, or edge cases — what this does or does NOT cover.
